CRT|/cr.rel.rows/1/1: Crystalline waterproofing with {IC}; leaks plugged with {F20}; cracks, holes and coves with {IM} — four applications from the inside.
CRT|/cr.rel.rows/2/1: {BIS540} and {BIS16} level pool tank walls and model pool edges; {HSF} is the bond coat for the screed.
CRT|/cr.cta.desc: Good Startup LTD. supplies the SCHOMBURG concrete restoration system in Taiwan and supports specification, quantities and application.
CRT|/cr.hero.alt: Sample panel of the concrete restoration system: each step of the build-up is left visible beside the next one
CRT|/cr.sub0/1: prepared concrete: firm, grippy, load-bearing, pore open; matt damp at the time of application
CRT|/cr.sub0w/1: chased crack and cove zone: roughened, cleaned with pressure water, matt damp, no puddles
CRT|/cr.cap.fill1: First layer of {BIS540}: up to 20 mm per application step; greater thicknesses are built up in several layers.
CRT|/cr.cap.scratch: Scratch coat: the same mortar {BIS16}, pressed into the matt damp substrate, closes pores and blowholes.
CRT|/cr.cap.felt: After a corresponding waiting time the surface is finished with a felt or sponge board.
CRT|/cr.cap.cureW: The crystals grow into the capillaries and into the crack from the treated side. Keep damp for at least 3 days.

CRT|/cr.m3d.microNote: Micro scale: schematic close-up of a sectioned sample at the repair interface, not to scale. Each stage plays as a short animation.
CRT|/cr.m3d.microSub/steel: Micro scale shows the interface itself: the rusting steel in carbonated cement paste, the blasted steel, the two coats of {HSF}, the bond coat brushed into the pores, the repair mortar and the fine smoothing mortar growing on it, layer by layer.
CRT|/cr.m3d.microSub/breakout: Micro scale shows the broken concrete surface with its pores, the bond coat brushed into them, and the repair mortar and the fine smoothing mortar growing on it, layer by layer.
CRT|/cr.m3d.microSub/surface: Micro scale shows the blowholes in the concrete skin, the scratch coat pressed into them, the fine smoothing mortar and its felt finish.
CRT|/cr.m3d.microSub/water: Micro scale shows the crack in the cement paste conducting water, the plug, the crystalline slurry, the mortar in the chase and the crystals growing into capillaries and crack.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/steel/0/1: {HSF} on the de-rusted steel (SA 2.5): two brush coats, the second after approx. 2 hours. The repair mortar follows approx. 6 hours after the second coat.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/steel/1/0: Bond coat and mortar, wet in wet
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/steel/1/1: {HSF} is brushed into the matt damp substrate, down to the pores. {BIS540} is applied while the bond coat is still wet, compacted and levelled flush.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/steel/2/1: Up to 20 mm per application step, greater thicknesses in several layers. {BIS16} closes the surface with 1–6 mm. Keep the mortar damp for at least 3–5 days.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/breakout/0/1: Loose parts are removed and the substrate is blasted until it is firm, grippy, load-bearing and pore open; the edges are cut square, not feathered.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/breakout/1/0: Bond coat and mortar, wet in wet
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/breakout/1/1: {HSF} is brushed into the matt damp substrate, down to the pores. {BIS540} follows while the bond coat is still wet, in steps of up to 20 mm.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/breakout/2/1: {BIS16} closes the surface with 1–6 mm after 24 hours at the earliest. Keep the mortar damp for at least 3–5 days.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/surface/0/1: On the matt damp substrate {BIS16} is first applied as a scratch coat that fills pores and blowholes, then in the layer thickness wanted.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/surface/1/0: 1–6 mm, struck off within the pot life
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/surface/1/1: Up to 6 mm per application step. Striking off with float or trowel within approx. 60 minutes; felt or sponge finish after a corresponding waiting time.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/surface/2/1: Protect from rapid drying: keep damp for at least 3–5 days; a cementitious waterproofing slurry can follow after approx. 24 hours.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/water/0/1: Running water is stopped with FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T; the crack is chased to approx. 20 × 25 mm, U-shaped, and the substrate is roughened and cleaned with pressure water.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/water/1/1: The flanks are screened with {IC}; {IM} follows wet in wet, flush in the chase and as a coved fillet of approx. 4 cm at the wall–floor joint.
CRT|/cr.m3d.co/water/2/1: After 1–3 hours {IM} is reworked with {IC}. The crystals grow into the capillaries; keep damp for at least 3 days.
CRT|/cr.m3d.callouts/0/1: {HSF} on the de-rusted steel (SA 2.5): two brush coats, the second after approx. 2 hours. The repair mortar follows approx. 6 hours after the second coat.
CRT|/cr.m3d.callouts/1/0: Bond coat and mortar, wet in wet
CRT|/cr.m3d.callouts/1/1: {HSF} is brushed into the matt damp substrate, down to the pores. {BIS540} is applied while the bond coat is still wet, compacted and levelled flush.
CRT|/cr.m3d.callouts/2/1: Up to 20 mm per application step, greater thicknesses in several layers. {BIS16} closes the surface with 1–6 mm. Keep the mortar damp for at least 3–5 days.

CRP_T|/BIS540/sub: Cementitious repair mortar for breakage points of 5 – 40 mm
CRP_T|/BIS540/role: The repair mortar. It re-profiles the breakout, wet in wet into the bond coat, in steps of up to 20 mm.
CRP_T|/BIS540/areas/1: for levelling pool tank walls, as well as modelling pool edges in swimming pools
CRP_T|/BIS540/adv/2: frost proof and resistant to thaw
CRP_T|/BIS540/data/12/0: Max. layer thickness per application step
CRP_T|/BIS540/data/16/1: class R4; adhesion ≥ 2.0 N/mm²; capillary water absorption ≤ 0.5 kg·m⁻²·h⁻⁰·⁵; resistance to carbonation passed
CRP_T|/BIS540/data/17/1: cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 12 months
CRP_T|/BIS16/sub: Cementitious fine smoothing mortar for breakage points of 1–6 mm
CRP_T|/BIS16/role: The fine smoothing mortar. It closes pores and blowholes and levels the repaired area, 1–6 mm.
CRP_T|/BIS16/areas/1: for levelling pool tank walls, as well as modelling pool edges in swimming pools
CRP_T|/BIS16/adv/2: frost proof and resistant to thaw
CRP_T|/BIS16/data/10/0: Max. layer thickness per application step
CRP_T|/BIS16/data/14/1: class R2; adhesion ≥ 0.8 N/mm²; capillary water absorption ≤ 0.5 kg·m⁻²·h⁻⁰·⁵; resistance to carbonation passed
CRP_T|/BIS16/data/15/1: cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 12 months
CRP_T|/IM/sub: Crystalline repair mortar for concrete, waterproofing
CRP_T|/IM/role: The waterproofing repair mortar. It fills chased cracks and holes and forms coved fillets, together with the crystalline slurry {IC}.
CRP_T|/IM/areas/0: for water tight filling of open cracks and holes
CRP_T|/IM/adv/4: can also be used on damp substrate
CRP_T|/IM/feat/1: increased active crack healing in concrete
CRP_T|/IM/data/7/0: Max. layer thickness per application step
CRP_T|/IM/data/11/1: cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 18 months
CRP_T|/HSF/sub: Flexible contact / bonding slurry and corrosion protection
CRP_T|/HSF/role: Two tasks in the system: corrosion protection on the de-rusted reinforcement, and the bond coat under the repair mortar.
CRP_T|/HSF/areas/0: as a cementitious bond coat on concrete substrates and repair mortars
CRP_T|/HSF/areas/1: as corrosive protection for exposed and abraded reinforcement bars
CRP_T|/HSF/areas/2: as a bond coat in concrete restoration
CRP_T|/HSF/areas/3: as a contact and bonding slurry for laying tiles and boards with the thick-bed method
CRP_T|/HSF/areas/4: as a bond coat for cement bonded screeds
CRP_T|/HSF/areas/5: for walls, ceilings, floors; for interior and exterior use
CRP_T|/HSF/adv/0: frost proof and resistant to thaw
CRP_T|/HSF/data/6/0: Water addition, contact and bonding slurry
CRP_T|/HSF/data/7/1: approx. 3 minutes, mix again after an activation time of 5 minutes
CRP_T|/HSF/data/10/0: Max. layer thickness per application step
CRP_T|/HSF/data/11/1: approx. 1–2 kg/m²; as bond coat approx. 1.5 kg/m² per mm; as corrosion protection approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm
CRP_T|/HSF/data/12/1: cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 12 months
CR_STEPS|/assess/short: An expert or structural engineer checks the current state before any restoration measure.
CR_STEPS|/assess/overview: Before any concrete restoration measures, the current state must generally be checked by an expert and/or structural engineer. The test report must be made available to the processor before starting the restoration measures.
CR_STEPS|/assess/points/0: cause and extent of the damage: carbonation, chlorides, cover, cross-section of the reinforcement
CR_STEPS|/assess/points/1: the test report decides the repair principle and the extent of the breakout
CR_STEPS|/assess/points/2: protect surfaces that are not to be treated
CR_STEPS|/prep/title: Break out and prepare the substrate
CR_STEPS|/prep/short: Remove everything loose; blast the substrate until it is firm, grippy, load-bearing and pore open.
CR_STEPS|/prep/overview: If no previous concrete restoration work has been carried out, a substrate preparation is required, e.g. granulate or shot blasting or ultra-high pressure water jetting (500–2000 bar).
CR_STEPS|/prep/points/0: requirement for the substrate: firm, grippy, load-bearing, pore open, free of adhesion inhibiting substances
